description: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity, labeled as “Per-Output”. The horizontal axis represents “Sparsity Rate”, with categories labeled 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, presented in ascending order. The vertical axis represents “Perplexity”, using a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick labels at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. Two bars are present for each sparsity rate, colored blue and orange, representing different conditions as indicated by the “Per-Output” legend. For the 10% sparsity rate, the blue bar extends to approximately 2, while the orange bar extends to approximately 2.2. At the 80% sparsity rate, the blue bar reaches approximately 950, and the orange bar reaches approximately 1000. The heights of the bars generally increase with increasing sparsity rate, with the orange bars consistently taller than the blue bars across all sparsity rates. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
